cudssHandle_t.doc:
The structure holds the cuDSS library context (device properties, system information, execution controls like `cudaStream_t`, etc.).

The handle must be initialized prior to calling any other cuDSS API with [`cudssCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreate "cudssCreate") or [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg").
The handle must be destroyed to free up resources after using cuDSS with [`cudssDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdestroy "cudssDestroy").

cudssMatrix_t.doc:
The structure is a lightweight wrapper around standard dense/sparse matrix parameters and does not own any data arrays.
Matrix objects are used to pass matrix of the linear system, as well as solution and right-hand side (even if these are in fact vectors).
Currently, cuDSS matrix objects can have either one of the two underlying matrix formats: dense and 3-array CSR (sparse). Additionally,
they can represent non-uniform batches of matrices or distributed (in the MGMN mode).

Matrix objects should be created via [`cudssMatrixCreateDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatedn "cudssMatrixCreateDn") (for dense matrices) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchdn "cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn") (for a batch of dense matrices) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatecsr "cudssMatrixCreateCsr") (for sparse matrices in CSR format) or
[`cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchcsr "cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr") (for a batch of sparse matrices in CSR format). After use, matrix objects should be destroyed
via [`cudssMatrixDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixdestroy "cudssMatrixDestroy"). For distributed matrices, one can additionally call [`cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetdistributionrow1d "cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d") to define how the matrix is distributed.

Matrix objects can be modified after creation via [`cudssMatrixSetValues()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetvalues "cudssMatrixSetValues") and [`cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetcsrpointers "cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers") (and similar APIs for batches).

Information can be retrieved from a matrix object by calling [`cudssMatrixGetFormat()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetformat "cudssMatrixGetFormat") followed by either [`cudssMatrixGetDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetdn "cudssMatrixGetDn") or [`cudssMatrixGetCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixgetcsr "cudssMatrixGetCsr") depending on the format returned.

cudssData_t.doc:
The structure holds internal data (e.g., factors related data structures) as well as pointers to user-provided data.
A single object of this type should be associated with solving a specific linear system.
If multiple systems with the same datatype(!) are solved consecutively the object can be re-used (all necessary internal buffers will be re-created per necessity).

Note: by default, the library allocates device memory required for performing LU factorization and storing the LU factors internally. All data buffers are of this kind are kept inside the data object.
To change this default behavior, one can set a [`cudssDeviceMemHandler_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdevicememhandler-t "cudssDeviceMemHandler_t") which will then be used for allocating device memory inside the solver.

The object should be created via [`cudssDataCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdatacreate "cudssDataCreate") and destroyed via [`cudssDataDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdatadestroy "cudssDataDestroy").

During execution of any of the stages [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"), configuration settings of the solver are read from `cudssConfig_t` and thus affect the execution and internal data stored in the `cudssData_t` object.

Data parameters can be updated or retrieved by calling [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") or [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") respectively.

cudssConfig_t.doc:
The structure stores configuration settings for the solver. This object is a lightweight (host-side) wrapper around common solver settings. While it can be re-used for solving different linear systems, it is recommended to have one per linear system.

The object should be created via [`cudssConfigCreate()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigcreate "cudssConfigCreate") and destroyed via [`cudssConfigDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigdestroy "cudssConfigDestroy").

During execution of any of the stages [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"), configuration settings of the solver are read from `cudssConfig_t` and thus affect the execution.

Configuration settings can be updated or retrieved by calling [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") or [`cudssConfigGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigget "cudssConfigGet") respectively.
Note: certain settings need to be set before a corresponding solver stage is executed (e.g., reordering algorithm must be set prior to the phase [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`]).

cudssDeviceMemHandler_t.doc:
This structure holds information about the user-provided, stream-ordered device memory pool (mempool).

The object can be created by setting the struct members described below.

Once created, a device memory handler can be set for the cuDSS library handle via [`cudssSetDeviceMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetdevicememhandler "cudssSetDeviceMemHandler").

Once set for the cuDSS library handle, information about the set device memory handler can be retrieved via [`cudssGetDeviceMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssgetdevicememhandler "cudssGetDeviceMemHandler").

`char name[CUDSS_ALLOCATOR_NAME_LEN]`

The name of the provided mempool (must not exceed 64 characters).

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool/context object.

device_alloc.signature: int device_alloc(void * ctx, void * * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
device_alloc.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for allocating device memory of size on `stream`.

The allocated memory should be made accessible to the current device (or more precisely, to the current CUDA context bound to the library handle).

This interface supports any stream-ordered memory allocator `ctx`. Upon success, the allocated memory can be immediately used on the given stream by any operations enqueued/ordered on the same stream after this call.

It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure a proper stream order is established.

The allocated memory should be at least 256-byte aligned.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: On success, a pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The amount of memory in bytes to be allocated.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream on which the memory is allocated (and the stream order is established).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

device_free.signature: int device_free(void * ctx, void * ptr, size_t size, cudaStream_t stream)
device_free.doc:
A function pointer to the user-provided routine for deallocating device memory of `size` on `stream`.

This interface supports any stream-ordered memory allocator. Upon success, any subsequent accesses (of the memory pointed to by the pointer `ptr`)
ordered after this call are undefined behaviors.

It is the caller’s responsibility to ensure a proper stream order is established.

If the arguments `ctx` and `size` are not the same as those passed to `device_alloc` to allocate the memory pointed to by `ptr`, the behavior is undefined.

The argument `stream` need not be identical to the one used for allocating `ptr`, as long as the stream order is correctly established. The behavior is undefined if this assumption is not held.

ctx.doc: A pointer to the user-owned mempool object.

ptr.doc: The pointer to the allocated buffer.

size.doc: The size of the allocated memory.

stream.doc: The CUDA stream on which the memory is deallocated (and the stream order is established).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudss_fp64mp2_t.doc:
The structure represents an extended-precision (double-double) floating-point value corresponding to [`CUDSS_R_64F_64F`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdatatype-t "CUDSS_R_64F_64F").

The value is stored as the unevaluated sum of two `double` components `hi + lo` and must be 16-byte aligned.

hi.doc: High-order part of the extended-precision value.

lo.doc: Low-order part of the extended-precision value.

cudssLoggerCallback_t.doc: A callback function pointer type for logging.

functionName.doc: Name of the API function that generated the log.

cudssDataType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the data type of values, offsets and indices used in cuDSS matrix objects and API calls.

The enumerator values for real and complex floating-point types alias the corresponding `cudaDataType_t` values and are interchangeable with them.

CUDSS_DATA_TYPE_UNSET.doc: Sentinel value indicating an uninitialized or unset data type. Not a valid value for user-facing API calls.

CUDSS_R_64F_64F.doc: 128-bit real double-double floating-point ([`cudss_fp64mp2_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudss-fp64mp2-t "cudss_fp64mp2_t")). This extended-precision type stores a value as the unevaluated sum of two `double` values (hi + lo).

CUDSS_R_32I.doc: 32-bit signed integer (`int32_t`). Used for index and offset arrays.

CUDSS_R_64I.doc: 64-bit signed integer (`int64_t`). Used for index and offset arrays.

cudssStatus_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies possible status values (on the host) which can be returned from calls to cuDSS routines.

Note: device side failures are returned via [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO") from [`cudssDataParam_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "cudssDataParam_t").

CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED.doc: One of the input operands was not properly initialized prior to the call to a cuDSS routine. This can usually be one of the opaque objects like [`cudssHandle_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsshandle-t "cudssHandle_t"), [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") or others.

CUDSS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.doc: Resource allocation failed inside the cuDSS library. This is usually caused by a device memory allocation (cudaMalloc()) or by a host memory allocation failure.

CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE.doc: An incorrect value or parameter was passed to the function (a negative vector size, or a NULL pointer for a must-have buffer, for example).

CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: An unsupported (but otherwise reasonable) parameter was passed to the function.

CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED.doc: The GPU program failed to execute. This is often caused by a launch failure of the kernel on the GPU, which can be caused by multiple reasons.

CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED.doc: Iterative refinement failed to meet the requested convergence tolerance. In this case, the iterations were performed and the refined solution is still accessible.

cudssConfigParam_t.doc: The enumerator specifies possible names of solver configuration settings. For each setting there is a matching type to be used in [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") or [`cudssConfigGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigget "cudssConfigGet").

CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the reordering phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`] - let the library choose (typically nested dissection).
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] - a customized nested dissection algorithm based on METIS.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] - a custom combination of block triangular reordering and COLAMD algorithms which can be used together with global pivoting to increase solution pivots.
  When this option is used for reordering, cuDSS uses an appropriate custom factorization algorithm (without the need to change the factorization setting [`CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG")).
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] - similar to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] in that it implies using a special factorization algorithm which is tailored for a block-triangular representation but uses a trivial block structure.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`] - an approximate minimum degree (AMD) reordering.
* [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE`] - uses natural (identity) order for the internal ordering when no user permutation is supplied.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are only supported for general (non-symmetric or non-hermitian) matrices.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] uses an upper bound on the number of non-zero entries in the factors.
If this bound appears to be not sufficient during the factorization phase, a runtime device error is returned (which can be checked by synchronizing the stream and calling `cudssDataGet()` with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO") which will output the device error).
In order to set a non-default upper bound, one should call `cudssConfigSet()` with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ") setting.

Note: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`] does not support the matrix index type `int64_t`.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "cudssReorderingAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the factorization phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT`] - the default factorization algorithm.
  This option chooses the best fitting factorization algorithm based on the choice of the reordering algorithm and sparsity structure produced by it.
  It is not recommended to use other options.
* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] - multiblock factorization algorithm. Starting with cudss 0.8.0, this option is supported only for real double data type. Suggested for use with extremely sparse matrices.
* [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_GENERAL`] - general factorization algorithm.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssfactorizationalg-t "cudssFactorizationAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for the solving phase. Supported options are:

* [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT`] - the default solve algorithm.
* [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL`] - triangular solve only (forward/back substitution using existing L/U factors, without modifying them).

Associated parameter type: [`cudssSolveAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsssolvealg-t "cudssSolveAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT`], currently equivalent to [`cudssSolveAlg_t::CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG.doc:
Algorithm for pivot epsilon calculation. When a pivot has magnitude smaller than the pivot epsilon threshold (see the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON`]), it is replaced by an appropriately signed value derived from the epsilon; the chosen algorithm controls how that value is computed.

Supported options are:

* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT`] - Default behavior pre-selected by the library, currently equivalent to [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`].
* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`] - Pivots with magnitude smaller than epsilon will be replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon scaled by the maximum element in the corresponding row and column of the original matrix.
* [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`] - Pivots with magnitude smaller than epsilon will be replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon (no scaling).

Note: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`] is not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG") is set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`].

Associated parameter type: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivotepsilonalg-t "cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG.doc:
Matching is an optional preprocessing step which computes a (non-symmetric column) permutation to put larger values on the diagonal which often improves the accuracy of the solution.
This permutation is then combined with the permutation from the reordering.
Set to [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE") to disable matching; for any other value, matching is enabled.
While matching often reduces the number of perturbed pivots and improves accuracy of the solution
(especially for ill-conditioned and badly scaled matrices) there are no guarantees that the accuracy will improve.
Enabling matching brings an overhead during the analysis step and changes the non-zero pattern of the factors and therefore, can slow down factorization and solve.

Note: matching routines require their internal workspace size to fit into the limit of 32-bit integers. The workspace limit depend on the choice of the matching algorithm.
The biggest requirement among them is to have `10 * nrows + nnz` < `INT_MAX` (`nrows` and `nnz` for the input matrix without accounting for symmetry).

Supported options are:

* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] - matching is disabled.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_COUNT`] - this option is based on `job = 1` from MC64 algorithm (HSL).
  Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the permuted matrix has as many entries on its diagonal as possible. The values on the diagonal are of arbitrary size.
  Note: this option does not use matrix values and thus can actually make the accuracy worse. It is not recommended to use this algorithm for matching unless there is a justified need.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`] - this option is based on `job = 2` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the smallest value on the diagonal of the permuted matrix is maximized.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG_ALT`] - this option is based on `job = 3` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the smallest value on the diagonal of the permuted matrix is maximized.
  This algorithm is different from the one used for [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`].
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_SUM`] - this option is based on `job = 4` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the sum of the diagonal entries of the permuted matrix is maximized.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`] - this option is based on `job = 5` from MC64 algorithm (HSL). Computes a column permutation of the matrix so that the product of the diagonal entries of the permuted matrix is maximized.
  In addition, this algorithm computes the row/col scaling vectors which can further improve accuracy of the solution.
* [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`] - the library selects the alg to apply, currently the same as [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`] (matching with scaling, requires matrix values, the most robust option).

Note: one of the options, [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`], computes scaling vectors in addition to the matching permutation. This option is considered to be the most impactful and it is recommended to use this option if accuracy of the solution needs to be improved.
However, this option requires matrix values to be present during the analysis step.

Note: matching is not supported for [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms (which use global pivoting to make the solution more accurate) or for matrices with type [`cudssDataType_t::CUDSS_R_64F_64F`] or for distributed matrices.

Associated parameter type: [`cudssMatchingAlg_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "cudssMatchingAlg_t")

Default value: [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] (matching disabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_MODE.doc:
Potential modifier on the system matrix (e.g. transpose or conjugate transpose)

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (no modifier).

Other values are not supported.

CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS.doc:
Maximum number of steps during the iterative refinement. Refer to [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") for the details.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL.doc:
Iterative refinement tolerance.

When users set both [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") > 0 and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") > 0,
the solver performs iterative refinement with convergence checking.

In each iteration, the relative residual norm is computed as $||r||_2 / ||b||_2$ where $r = b - Ax$.

The refinement terminates early if the residual norm is less than the specified tolerance.

If [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL") = 0 and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") > 0,
exactly [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") iterations are performed without convergence checking.

The actual number of iterations performed can be retrieved via [`CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS").
If the tolerance is not met after all iterations, [`CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_IR_FAILED") is returned.

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `0.0` (tolerance checking disabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_TYPE.doc:
Type of pivoting

The exact meaning of this parameter depends on the choice of the reordering algorithm which can be changed through [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").
For [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] the parameter refers to the global pivoting, while for [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] and others it refers to the partial 1x1 pivoting procedure.

Note that in the latter case, if the matrix type is symmetric but not positive-definite, then the pivoting is also symmetric and the pivot is searched for on the diagonal of the block, if only the pivot type is not equal to [`cudssPivotType_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_NONE`].

For more details, see the description of the [pivoting strategies](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#numerical-pivoting).

Associated parameter type: [`cudssPivotType_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "cudssPivotType_t")

Default value: [`cudssPivotType_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO`].

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_THRESHOLD.doc:
Pivoting threshold $p_{threshold}$ which is used to determine if diagonal element is subject to pivoting and will be swapped with the maximum element in the row (or column) depending on the [type of pivoting](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivottype-t).
The diagonal element will be swapped if:
$p_{threshold} \cdot max_{(sub)row \\, or \\, col} |a_{ij}| \geq |a_{ii}|$

For more details, see the description of the [pivoting strategies](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#numerical-pivoting).

Note: this parameter is only supported when reordering algorithm is set to [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `1.0`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON.doc:
Pivoting epsilon.

By default, this is the absolute value to test and replace small diagonal elements encountered during numerical factorization.

In case [`CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG") is set to [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED`], this value will be additionally scaled (see more details in the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`]).

Associated parameter type: `double`

Default value: `1e-5` for single precision and `1e-13` for double precision.

CUDSS_CONFIG_MAX_LU_NNZ.doc:
Upper limit on the number of nonzero entries in LU factors. This is only relevant for non-symmetric matrices and reordering algorithm set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`].
If the number of non-zero entries in L and U exceeds the set limit, a runtime error happen. See also the note for [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] in the table entry for [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

Default value: `-1` (then the parameter value is ignored and cuDSS uses an estimate of `100 nnz` where `nnz` is the number of non-zero entries in the input matrix).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE.doc:
Memory mode: `0` (default = device-only) or `1` (hybrid = host/device).

Note: Hybrid host/device memory mode should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS")).
If the decision to use the hybrid mode is done after the analysis phase, the hybrid memory mode should be enabled and analysis phase must be re-done (which is sub-optimal).

Note: Unlike the hybrid host/device execution mode (see [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE")) which controls where compute kernels are executed, the hybrid memory mode
only allows cuDSS to keep a part of the factor values (internal data) on the host and always uses the GPU for factorization and solve.

For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering, or, when [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] is used for the factorization.

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_LIMIT.doc:
User-defined device memory limit (number of bytes) for the hybrid memory mode.

This setting only affects execution when the hybrid host/device memory mode is enabled.
For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")), this value must be set for each device separately by calling `cudaSetDevice()` prior to [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet")

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

Default value: `-1` (use the internal default heuristic).

CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_CUDA_REGISTER_MEMORY.doc:
A flag to enable or disable usage of `cudaHostRegister()` by cuDSS hybrid host/device memory mode. Since the hybrid memory mode of cuDSS uses host memory to store the factors,
it can use `cudaHostRegister()` (if the HW supports it) to speedup associated host-to-device and device-to-host memory transfers.
However, registering host memory has limitations and in some cases might lead to slowdowns. If the flag is set to `0`, cuDSS will not attempt to use `cudaHostRegister()` even if the HW supports it.
This setting only affects execution when the hybrid memory mode is enabled. For more details, see [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1` (use `cudaHostRegister()` if the device supports it).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HOST_NTHREADS.doc:
Number of threads to be used by cuDSS in [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).
This setting only affects execution when the multi-threaded mode is enabled.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `-1` (use number of threads returned by `cudssGetMaxThreads()`).

CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE.doc:
Execute mode: `0` (default = device-only) or `1` (hybrid = host/device).
Hybrid execute mode allows cuDSS to perform calculations on both GPU and CPU.
Currently it is used to speed up execution parts with low parallelization capacity.

Note: Reordering part of the analysis step is performed on CPU regardless of execute mode value.

Note: Hybrid execute mode should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`]).

Note: Unlike the hybrid execution mode which controls where compute kernels are executed
(and allows greater flexibility in placement of the input data), the hybrid host/device memory mode [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") only allows cuDSS to keep part of the factor values (internal data)
on the host while only the GPU is used for factorization and solve.

Note: If hybrid execute mode is enabled, input matrix, right hand side and solution can be host memory pointers.

For more details, see the [Hybrid host/device execute mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode) feature.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Note: For `nrhs > 1`, any non-one value must be set before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS")); the exact value used during solve does not need to match.

Note: It is strongly recommended to enable the threading layer ([`cudssSetThreadingLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetthreadinglayer "cudssSetThreadingLayer")) when hybrid execute mode is active, as all analysis step computations are enhanced by multi-threading. Expect significant performance improvements, especially for small and medium-sized matrices.

Default value: `0` (disabled). Currently not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") is used.
Also not supported when [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE") is enabled, or, when `batchCount` is greater than 1, or when right-hand side and/or solution have a non-trivial leading dimension.

CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS.doc:
Minimum number of levels for the nested dissection reordering. The value for this parameter should be a positive integer.
Additionally, for the [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) the number of levels will be automatically increased (if needed) to satisfy the requirement: $2^{n_{levels}-1} \geq n_{proc}$
where $n_{proc}$ is the number of processes in the communicator. This setting only works when reordering algorithm is [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`] (which is also [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT`]).

Note: This is considered an advanced performance knob and it is recommended to use a non-default value only when optimizing for performance. Typical values to try should not be too far from the default value, e.g. from the range 8 - 11.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `10`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_UBFACTOR.doc:
Controls the balance of the nested dissection partition tree. The value represents the allowed percentage of imbalance between the two children at each level of the partition tree. Possible values are from 1 to 100.

Note: Smaller values produce a more balanced partition tree. For [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) and [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode), it is recommended to use smaller values in the range 2 to 5.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `20`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE.doc:
The number of matrices in a uniform batch of systems to be processed by cuDSS. Uniform batch of matrices is defined as a batch of matrices with the same non-zero pattern but potentially different values.
To create a uniform batch of matrices (unlike a non-uniform batch) one can simply use the usual [`cudssMatrixCreateCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatecsr "cudssMatrixCreateCsr") or [`cudssMatrixCreateDn()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatedn "cudssMatrixCreateDn")
with the only change: as a pointer to the matrix values one should provide a buffer which holds values for all matrices in the batch.
Thus, it should have `nnz * CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE` elements
for sparse matrices (`csr_values` only) and `nrows * ncols * CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE` elements for dense matrices.

Note: a single system can be viewed as a uniform batch with [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] set to 1.

There are two ways how cuDSS can process a uniform batch based on the value of the [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX"): either factorizing (or solving) all matrices at once or just one at a time.

For details, see the description of [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`].

Note: [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`] must be set before calling [`cudssPhase_t::CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`].

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1`.

Currently not supported when either [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode)) or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode))
are enabled, or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) is used, or with [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms.

CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX.doc:
`-1` or a 0-based index of matrix in a uniform batch which will be processed during factorization or solve phase.
Special value of `-1` can be used to tell cuDSS to process all matrices in the uniform batch at once.

Note: [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] must be less than [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_SIZE").

Note: if [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] is set then cuDSS will treat the input sparse matrix, right hand side and solution as regular matrices (with just one set of values).
Thus, it allows to process a uniform batch of matrices one by one while re-using the result of the analysis and keeping corresponding factors for all matrices in a single `cudssData_t` object.

Note: [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`] can be set after [`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION"), in that case one could solve only one specific system

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `-1`

Currently not supported when either [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode)) or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode))
are enabled, or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) is used, or with [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms.

CUDSS_CONFIG_USE_SUPERPANELS.doc:
Use superpanel optimization: `1` (default = enabled) or `0` (disabled).

Note: superpanel optimization should be enabled before the analysis phase ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") with [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS")).
If the decision to use the superpanel optimization mode is done after the analysis phase, the superpanel optimization should be enabled and analysis phase must be re-done which is sub-optimal).

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1` (enabled).

CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT.doc:
Device count in case of multiple device (see [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg"))

Note: Maximum supported device count is 16

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `1`.

CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES.doc:
A list of device indices as an integer array.

Note: The calling device must be equal to the first device index from `device_indices` or `0` (if `device_indices` were `NULL` in the required prior call to [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg"))

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `NULL` (cuDSS will use devices from 0 to `device_count - 1`).

CUDSS_CONFIG_SCHUR_MODE.doc:
Schur complement mode: `0` (default = disabled) or `1` (enabled).

For more details regarding the Schur complement feature, see [Schur complement feature](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#schur-complement).

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering, when [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) or [multi-GPU mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) is used,
or, when [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK`] is used for the factorization. It is also not supported for uniform and non-uniform batches, or when matching is enabled.

CUDSS_CONFIG_DETERMINISTIC_MODE.doc:
Enable deterministic mode.
In deterministic mode, cuDSS is guaranteed to provide the bit-wise identical result at every run when executed on GPUs with the same architecture
and the same number of SMs (assuming the input data and solver settings are also bit-wise identical).

Note: in deterministic mode cuDSS uses a different set of kernels which often might be slower than the kernels used in the default mode.

Associated parameter type: `int`

Default value: `0` (disabled).

Currently the feature is supported only for single-gpu, single rhs, and with both hybrid host/device memory mode ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE")) and hybrid host/device execute mode ([`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE")) disabled.
Also, this feature does not support iterative refinement or reordering algorithms [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

cudssDataParam_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies possible parameter names which can set or get in the [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t") object. For each parameter name
there is an associated type to be used in [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") or [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet"). Each parameter
name is marked with “in” or “out” depending on whether a parameter can be only set, get or be involved in both.

CUDSS_DATA_INFO.doc:
By default, this parameter can be used to detect device-side asynchronous errors (primarily, during factorization and solve).
However, in the special case, when in [hybrid host/device execute mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode), factorization is done on the host at least partially,
this parameter can be used to retrieve host-side errors. In case execution is successful, the value is `0`.

Note: the error returned via [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_INFO`] is independent from the host side status of type [`cudssStatus_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssstatus-t "cudssStatus_t") returned by all cuDSS routines, including [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").
One of the noticeable use cases is when a matrix of the system is passed with an `mtype` for positive-definite matrices but it appears to have non-positive minors (at least numerically).
In this case, calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_INFO`] after the factorization phase will return the 1-based index of the first encountered non-positive minor.
Then one can set the device error back to zero via [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet"), and either change the matrix type or adjust the matrix values (to make the matrix positive-definite) and call the factorization phase again.

Note that the returned index is 1-based and is for the reordered matrix.
To get the corresponding original index, it should be combined with (inverse) permutation which can be extracted via [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") for [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW").

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int`.

CUDSS_DATA_LU_NNZ.doc:
Number of non-zero entries in LU factors.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns accumulated number over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`.

CUDSS_DATA_NPIVOTS.doc:
Number of pivots encountered during factorization.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_INERTIA.doc:
Positive and negative indices of inertia for the system matrix `A` (two integer values). Valid only for symmetric/Hermitian non positive-definite matrix types.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns the accumulated number over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW.doc:
Row permutation `P` after reordering such that `A[P,Q]` is factorized.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL.doc:
Column permutation `Q` after reordering such that `A[P,Q]` is factorized.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW.doc:
Final row permutation P (includes effects of both reordering and pivoting) which is applied to the original right-hand side of the system in the form $b_{new} = b_{old} \circ P$

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently supported only when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_COL.doc:
Final column permutation Q (includes effects of both reordering and pivoting) which is applied to transform the solution of the permuted system into the original solution $x_{old} = x_{new} \circ Q^{-1}$

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently supported only when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_PERM_MATCHING.doc:
Matching (column) permutation `Q` such that `A[:,Q]` is reordered and then factorized.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_DIAG.doc:
Diagonal of the factorized matrix. The diagonal is returned in the original matrix order, taking into account all permutations applied during matching, reordering, and pivoting.

Note: in case `batchCount` > 1 (non-uniform batch) [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") returns the accumulated values over all
matrices in the batch.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the values of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently supported only when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_ROW.doc:
Row scaling the factorized matrix (corresponding to the rows of the original matrix)

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: floating point for the absolute values of the matrix of the system (i.e., always real, either float or double)

Only supported when matching is enabled (i.e. [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") is not [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE")) and the chosen matching algorithm computes the scaling.

CUDSS_DATA_SCALE_COL.doc:
Column scaling the factorized matrix (corresponding to the columns of the original matrix).

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: floating point for the absolute values of the matrix of the system (i.e., always real, either float or double). Only supported when matching is enabled (i.e. [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG") is not [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE")) and the chosen matching algorithm computes the scaling.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM.doc:
User permutation to be used instead of running the reordering algorithms.
The user permutation can be disabled by providing a `NULL` with zero size with [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet").
The provided buffer should be an integer array of size `n`, where `n` is the number of rows/columns of the system matrix.
The integer type must match the one used for the system matrix.
The values should represent a valid permutation vector for the set $\\{ index base, ..., n - index base \\}$

Note: after [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") is called with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`], the data are copied into an internal buffer so that the user buffer can be deallocated or re-used.

Note: using this parameter in [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") in case `batchCount` > 1 is not supported.

Direction: in

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system

Currently not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] is used for reordering.

CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE.doc:
Nested Dissection (ND) partition tree information, also known as a separator tree or separator sizes, which are computed during the reordering phase and used for improving parallelization.
The number of elements in this array is $2^{n_{levels}} - 1$ with
$n_{levels}$ from [`CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_ND_NLEVELS"). It can be used in combination with
[`CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM") and [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE") for a matrix with the same sparsity structure.
This avoids regenerating the same reordering information while retaining the same performance for the factorization and solve phases.

See the [Nested Dissection Partition Tree](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#user-provided-nested-dissection-nd-partition-tree-data-saving-reordering) section for more details.

Direction: out

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_ND_PARTITION_TREE.doc:
User provided nested dissection (ND) partition tree information, which is used instead of running the reordering algorithm (therefore, saving runtime).
It must be used in combination with [`CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_USER_PERM") to have an effect.

See [`CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_ND_PARTITION_TREE") for the size and usage information. The user ND partition tree can be disabled by providing a `NULL` with zero size with [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet").

Note: While it is possible to construct this array outside cuDSS (e.g., extracting the so-called `sizes` array from METIS / ParMETIS), we recommend to only use this feature by extracting the ND partition tree from cuDSS,
followed by passing it back in subsequent calls.

Direction: in

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_MEMORY_ESTIMATES.doc:
Memory estimates (in bytes) for host and device memory required for the chosen memory mode.
The chosen memory mode is defined as the memory mode detected during the last executed analysis phase for the current `cudssData_t` object and the state of the corresponding `cudssConfigParam_t` object during the call.

See [`cudssConfigParam_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "cudssConfigParam_t") for more details.

Note: the returned memory estimate depends not just on the settings from `cudssConfig_t` object but also on the input matrix and rhs (specifically, nrhs)
so if the objects (or the config) change after the analysis phase, memory estimates might be not accurate anymore.

Values returned in the output array at position:
\* 0 - permanent device memory
\* 1 - peak device memory
\* 2 - permanent host memory
\* 3 - peak host memory
\* 4 - (if in hybrid memory mode) minimum device memory for the hybrid memory mode
\* 5 - (if in hybrid memory mode) maximum host memory for the hybrid memory mode
\* 6, … 15 - reserved for future use

This query must be done after the analysis phase and will return status [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`] if it cannot be processed.

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")) memory estimate will be done for the calling device only.
Thus, `cudaSetDevice()` must be called prior to `cudssDataGet()` to get memory estimate on corresponded device

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t[16]`.

CUDSS_DATA_HYBRID_DEVICE_MEMORY_MIN.doc:
Minimal amount of device memory (number of bytes) required in the hybrid memory mode. This query must be done after the analysis phase and will return status [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED`] if it cannot be processed.

Note: In case of multiple devices ([`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")), minimal memory will be returned for the calling device only.
Thus, `cudaSetDevice()` must be called prior to `cudssDataGet()` to get minimal memory on corresponding device

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

For more details, see the [Hybrid host/device memory mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode) feature.

CUDSS_DATA_FLOPS.doc:
Floating-point operation count for the factorization phase.

Note: the value is available after the [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") step.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`.

CUDSS_DATA_COMM_DEVICE.doc:
Device communicator for [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).
The actual type of the communicator must match the device communication backend of the [communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) which must be set via calling [`cudssSetCommLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetcommlayer "cudssSetCommLayer").
This communicator is used for communication involving device memory buffers.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `void*`

See [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) for further details.

CUDSS_DATA_COMM_HOST.doc:
Host communicator for [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).
The actual type of the communicator must match the host communication backend of the [communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) which must be set via calling [`cudssSetCommLayer()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetcommlayer "cudssSetCommLayer").
This communicator is used for communication involving host memory buffers.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `void*`

See [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) for further details.

CUDSS_DATA_NSUPERPANELS.doc:
Number of superpanels in the matrix.

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES.doc:
User-provided Schur complement indices. The provided buffer should be an integer array of size `n`, where `n` is the number of rows (columns) of the system matrix,
and the integer type should match the one used for the system matrix.
The values should be equal to `1` for the rows/columns which are part of the Schur complement and `0` for the rest.

Note: after [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") is called with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_SCHUR_INDICES`], the data are copied into an internal buffer so that the user buffer can be deallocated or re-used.

Direction: in

Memory: host or device

Associated parameter type: same as for the indices of the sparse matrix of the system.

CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_SHAPE.doc:
Shape of the Schur complement matrix as a triplet `(nrows, ncols, sparse nnz)`. The last entry is only relevant when the Schur complement needs to be exported as a sparse matrix
By querying with [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") with [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_SHAPE`], users can get the necessary allocation sizes for the Schur complement buffers
which can then be used to create a `cudssMatrix_t` object and passed back to cuDSS to fill in the Schur complement data via [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX").

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t[3]`.

CUDSS_DATA_SCHUR_MATRIX.doc:
Schur complement matrix as a `cudssMatrix_t` object.

Direction: in

Memory: host (with underlying buffers on host or device)

Associated parameter type: `cudssMatrix_t`

Note: the data type for matrix values, offsets and indices (if it is a sparse matrix) must be same as for the values, offsets and indices of the system matrix respectively.

Note: Schur complement matrix cannot be a distributed matrix. Also, Schur complement cannot be computed for matrix batches currently. For the dense Schur complement,
the layout must be column-major. For sparse Schur complement, the matrix type must be [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`] and the matrix view must be [`cudssMatrixViewType_t::CUDSS_MVIEW_FULL`].

CUDSS_DATA_USER_HOST_INTERRUPT.doc:
User-provided host interrupt pointer. Setting this pointer to a non-`NULL` value enables user interruption of cuDSS routines on the host.
Specifically, in the calls to [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute") cuDSS will perform checks on the host for the value of the pointer.
If it is non-zero, execution stops and cuDSS returns early (before the phase execution completes) with the status [`CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssstatus-t "CUDSS_STATUS_EXECUTION_FAILED").
To resume after an interruption, set the value at that location back to `0` and call again.
To remove the (small) overhead of checking for the host interruption, the interruption can be completely disabled by setting [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_USER_HOST_INTERRUPT`] to `NULL`.

Note: since most of device kernels inside cuDSS are launched asynchronously,
execution on the GPU may continue some time after the host execution has been interrupted.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Default value: `NULL` (user interruption disabled)

Associated parameter type: pointer to a 4-byte integer (e.g. `int32_t` or `int`).

Note: When setting the flag from another thread, the user must use an atomic store with release semantics so the library observes the write. A plain write to a non-atomic object from another thread is a data race and undefined behavior.

Note: `std::atomic<int>` (C++) or `_Atomic(int)*` (C) may be used when the object representation is a single 4-byte integer; the library does not guarantee correct behavior for all atomic types.

Note: The host interruption feature is not supported when [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) or [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) is used.
Also, reordering algorithms [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] do not support the user interrupt currently.

CUDSS_DATA_IR_N_STEPS.doc:
Actual number of iterative refinement steps performed

Direction: out

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int`

This parameter stores the actual number of iterative refinement iterations performed during the solve phase.

The value can be less than [`CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS") if user-specified convergence tolerance is reached.
The value is 0 if iterative refinement is disabled or if the initial solution already satisfies the tolerance.

CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK.doc:
A bitmask specifying the subset of problems to be factorized or solved in the uniform batch case. Each bit position corresponds to the index of a matrix in the uniform batch; setting a bit to `1` includes that matrix in the operation.

Note: [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`] can be used as an alternative to [`CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_UBATCH_INDEX") to select multiple specific problems from the batch in a single call.

Note: [`cudssDataParam_t::CUDSS_DATA_UBATCH_MASK`] can be set after [`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION"), in that case one could solve only a specific subset of systems.

Direction: in

Memory: host

Associated parameter type: `int64_t`

Default value: `-1` (all problems selected).

Currently not supported when either [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_MEMORY_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-memory-mode)) or [`CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_HYBRID_EXECUTE_MODE") (see [here](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode))
are enabled, or [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode) is used, or with [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] and [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] reordering algorithms.

cudssPhase_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the solver phases to be performed in the main cuDSS routine [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").
Phases can be combined with the binary OR operator (`|`) to specify multiple phases at once: `CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION | CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE`.

CUDSS_PHASE_SYMBOLIC_FACTORIZATION.doc:
Symbolic factorization

Note: it is not allowed to call symbolic factorization twice without calling the reordering phase in-between.

CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION.doc:
Numerical re-factorization.

Note: For now it is only used if the reordering algorithm is set to [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`]. Otherwise, it is the same as FACTORIZATION phase.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_FWD_PERM.doc:
Applying reordering permutation to the right hand side before the forward solve (forward substitution).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_FWD.doc:
Forward substitution sub-step of the solving phase.

Note: this phase includes the local permutation due to the partial pivoting.
To remove this effect, if undesired, one can use a combination of reordering and final permutation (see [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") and [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW")).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_DIAG.doc:
Diagonal solve sub-step of the solving phase (only needed for symmetric/Hermitian matrix types).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_BWD.doc:
Backward substitution sub-step of the solving phase.

Note: this phase includes the local permutation due to the partial pivoting.
To remove this effect, if undesired, one can use a combination of reordering and final permutation (see [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") and [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_ROW")).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_BWD_PERM.doc:
Applying inverse reordering permutation to the intermediate solution after the backward (backward substitution).
If matching (and scaling) is enabled, this phase also includes applying the inverse matching permutation and inverse scaling (as the matching permutation and scalings were used to modify the matrix before the factorization).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE_REFINEMENT.doc:
Iterative refinement (see configuration settings [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_N_STEPS`] and [`cudssConfigParam_t::CUDSS_CONFIG_IR_TOL`]).

Note: solve sub-phases are not supported when [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`] or [`cudssReorderingAlg_t::CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`] are used for reordering.

CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE.doc:
Full solving phase, combining all of the above (forward permutation + forward solve + diagonal solve + backward permutation + backward solve) and (optional) iterative refinement.

Note: combining the solve sub-phases should be preferred to calling sub-phases separately.

Note: Changing the sparse matrix for this phase is allowed but with restrictions, see limitations for [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

cudssMatrixFormat_t.doc: The enumerator specifies the underlying matrix formats inside a cuDSS matrix object.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_DENSE.doc: Matrix is dense (applied to a single matrix and a batch equally).

CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR.doc:
Matrix is in CSR format (applies to a single matrix and a batch equally)

Note: Only 3-array CSR is supported.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH.doc: Matrix object represents a batch of matrices.

CUDSS_MFORMAT_DISTRIBUTED.doc:
> Matrix object represents a distributed matrix (used in [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode))

Note: The format flags can be combined. E.g., creating a `cudssMatrix_t`
via [`cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatebatchcsr "cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr") would set both
[`cudssMatrixFormat_t::CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR`] and [`cudssMatrixFormat_t::CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH`] flags. One can check for a mixture of flags via bit-wise operations, e.g.
`CUDSS_MFORMAT_CSR | CUDSS_MFORMAT_BATCH` for a batch of CSR matrices.

cudssMatrixType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies available matrix types for sparse matrices.
Matrix type should be used to describe the properties of the underlying matrix storage.
Matrix type affects the decision about what type of factorization is computed by the solver.
E.g, when matrix type is one of the positive-definite types, checks for singular values on the diagonal is not done.

CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL.doc: General matrix [default] `LDU` factorization will be computed with optional local or global pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC.doc: Real symmetric matrix. `LDL^T` factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_HERMITIAN.doc: Complex Hermitian matrix. `LDL^H` factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting.

CUDSS_MTYPE_SPD.doc:
Symmetric positive-definite matrix Cholesky factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting

Note: if the matrix passed with this matrix type appears to have zero minors (at least numerically), one can get the 1-based index of the first encountered non-positive minor by
calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO"). As this would be a device-side error, the call to `cudssExecute()` may still return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`].

CUDSS_MTYPE_HPD.doc:
Hermitian positive-definite matrix Complex Cholesky factorization will be computed with optional local pivoting

Note: if the matrix passed with this matrix type appears to have zero minors (at least numerically), one can get the 1-based index of the first non-positive minor by
calling [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") with [`CUDSS_DATA_INFO`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_INFO"). As this would be a device-side error, the call to `cudssExecute()` may still return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`].

cudssMatrixViewType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies available matrix view types for sparse matrices. Matrix view defines how the matrix is treated by
the main cuDSS routine [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute"). E.g., to provide only upper-triangle data for a symmetric matrix
one can use as [`CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatrixtype-t "CUDSS_MTYPE_SYMMETRIC") as matrix type combined with [`CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatrixviewtype-t "CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER") as the matrix view.
If the accompanying matrix type is [`cudssMatrixType_t::CUDSS_MTYPE_GENERAL`], the matrix view is ignored.

CUDSS_MVIEW_LOWER.doc: Lower-triangular matrix (including the diagonal). All values above the main diagonal will be ignored.

CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER.doc: Upper-triangular matrix (including the diagonal). All values below the main diagonal will be ignored.

cudssIndexBase_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies indexing base (0 or 1) for sparse matrix indices (row start/end offsets and column indices).
Once set for a sparse matrix, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute")
will use the indexing base from the input sparse matrix for all index-related data (e.g. output from
[`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet") called with [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_ROW") or [`CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_PERM_REORDER_COL")).

cudssLayout_t.doc: The enumerator specifies dense matrix layout.

cudssReorderingAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the reordering algorithm for the analysis phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_REORDERING_ALG").

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_DEFAULT.doc:
The default algorithm for reordering (equivalent to
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION")).

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD.doc: Block triangular form (BTF) combined with COLAMD. Supports global pivoting.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD.doc: COLAMD with trivial block structure. Supports global pivoting.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION.doc: Nested dissection algorithm based on METIS.

CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NONE.doc: Uses natural (identity) order for the internal ordering when no user permutation is supplied.

cudssFactorizationAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the factorization algorithm for the numerical factorization phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_FACTORIZATION_ALG").

CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: The default factorization algorithm (equivalent to [`cudssFactorizationAlg_t::CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_GENERAL`], recommended).

CUDSS_FACTORIZATION_ALG_MULTIBLOCK.doc: Multiblock factorization algorithm. Supported only for real double data type (CUDA_R_64F). Suggested for use with extremely sparse matrices.

cudssSolveAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the algorithm for the solve phase.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_SOLVE_ALG").

CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: Let the library choose the solve algorithm (recommended).

CUDSS_SOLVE_ALG_GENERAL.doc: Triangular solve only: forward/back substitution using the existing L/U factors without modifying them.

cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the algorithm for pivot epsilon calculation when replacing small pivots during numerical factorization.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG").

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_DEFAULT.doc: The default pivot epsilon algorithm (same as [`cudssPivotEpsilonAlg_t::CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC`], recommended).

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_SCALED.doc: Pivots below the threshold are replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon scaled by the maximum element in the corresponding row and column of the original matrix. Not supported with [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").

CUDSS_PIVOT_EPSILON_ALG_STATIC.doc: Pivots below the threshold are replaced by the appropriately signed epsilon (no scaling). Recommended for most cases.

cudssMatchingAlg_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies the matching (column permutation) algorithm.

Used with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_MATCHING_ALG"). Except for [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_NONE`] and [`cudssMatchingAlg_t::CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO`], all options are based on the MC64 algorithm (HSL).

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_AUTO.doc: Same as [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT") (the most robust option). Matching with scaling; requires matrix values during analysis.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_COUNT.doc: Column permutation to maximize the number of diagonal entries (values arbitrary). MC64 JOB=1. Does not use matrix values; not recommended unless justified.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG.doc: Column permutation to maximize the smallest value on the diagonal. MC64 JOB=2.
