CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG_ALT.doc: Alternate algorithm to maximize the smallest value on the diagonal. MC64 JOB=3. May differ in performance from [`CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssmatchingalg-t "CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_MIN_DIAG").

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_SUM.doc: Column permutation to maximize the sum of diagonal entries. MC64 JOB=4.

CUDSS_MATCHING_ALG_MAX_DIAG_PRODUCT.doc: Column permutation to maximize the product of diagonal entries; also computes row/column scaling so that nonzero diagonal entries are 1 in absolute value and off-diagonal entries are ≤ 1. MC64 JOB=5. Most impactful for accuracy; requires matrix values during analysis.

cudssPivotType_t.doc: The enumerator specifies the pivoting strategy for numerical factorization.

CUDSS_PIVOT_AUTO.doc:
Automatic pivoting strategy [default]. Automatically selects the appropriate
pivot type based on the reordering algorithm and matrix type:

* For [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD"):

  + Symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices: Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL")
  + General matrices: Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK")
* For [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD"):
  Uses [`CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudsspivottype-t "CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL").

CUDSS_PIVOT_NONE.doc:
No pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).

CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_COL.doc:
Global column pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
Searches for pivot elements within entire columns of the sub-matrix.

CUDSS_PIVOT_GLOBAL_ROW.doc:
Global row pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") and [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD").
Searches for pivot elements within entire rows of the sub-matrix.

CUDSS_PIVOT_DIAGONAL.doc:
Diagonal pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).
For symmetric/Hermitian indefinite matrices, searches for pivot elements
only within the diagonal of the supernode.

CUDSS_PIVOT_LOCAL_BLOCK.doc:
Complete block pivoting. Used only with reordering algorithms
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_NESTED_DISSECTION") and
[`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_AMD") (MetisND and AMD).
For general matrices, searches for pivot elements within the entire
diagonal block of the supernode.

CUDSS_PIVOT_BUNCH_KAUFMAN.doc: Bunch-Kaufman pivoting. Reserved for future use. Currently not supported.

cudssDistributedInterface_t.doc:
This struct defines all communication primitives which need to be implemented
in (any) implementation of cuDSS communication layer, see for more details
[communication layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#communication-layer-library-in-cudss) and [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).

**Dual-backend structure**: Each communication primitive must be implemented **twice** —
once for device (GPU) memory buffers (function pointer name ending in `Device`) and once
for host (CPU) memory buffers (function pointer name ending in `Host`). Both variants have
identical signatures. cuDSS selects the appropriate variant based on the memory location of the
buffers at call time. For example, rank query has two function pointers: `cudssCommRankDevice`
and `cudssCommRankHost`.

Note: the `comm` argument to all functions is interpreted by the implementation based on the
underlying communication backend. E.g., for OpenMPI it should be treated as an `MPI_Comm`.

Note: functions with a `stream` argument must be stream-ordered. For GPU-aware backends like
OpenMPI, this implies performing an explicit `cudaStreamSynchronize()` inside the implementation.

cudssCommRankDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which returns the rank of the process in a communicator.

rank.doc: Rank of the calling process in the communicator.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssCommSizeDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which returns the number of processes in a communicator.

size.doc: Number of processes in the communicator.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssSendDevice.signature: int cudssSendDevice(const void * buffer, int count, cudssDataType_t datatype, int dest, int tag, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssSendDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which performs a blocking send.

buffer.doc: Initial address of the send buffer.

count.doc: Number of elements (of type `datatype`) to be sent.

datatype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be sent.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssRecvDevice.signature: int cudssRecvDevice(void * buffer, int count, cudssDataType_t datatype, int source, int tag, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssRecvDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which performs a blocking receive for a message.

buffer.doc: Initial address of the receive buffer.

count.doc: Number of elements (of type `datatype`) to be received.

datatype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be received.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssBcastDevice.signature: int cudssBcastDevice(void * buffer, int count, cudssDataType_t datatype, int root, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssBcastDevice.doc:
Function pointers to a routine which performs a broadcast from the `root` process

to all other processes of the communicator.

buffer.doc: Address of the buffer (send on root, receive on all other processes).

count.doc: Number of elements (of type `datatype`) to be broadcast.

datatype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be broadcast.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssReduceDevice.signature: int cudssReduceDevice(const void * sendbuf, void * recvbuf, int count, cudssDataType_t datatype, cudssOpType_t op, int root, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssReduceDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which performs a reduction to a single value on the root process.

recvbuf.doc: Address of the receive buffer (valid only at root).

count.doc: Number of elements (of type `datatype`) to be reduced.

datatype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be reduced.

op.doc: Type of the reduction operation to be performed, see [`cudssOpType_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssoptype-t "cudssOpType_t") for supported values.

root.doc: Rank of the root process (destination of the result).

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssAllreduceDevice.signature: int cudssAllreduceDevice(const void * sendbuf, void * recvbuf, int count, cudssDataType_t datatype, cudssOpType_t op, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssAllreduceDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which performs a reduction and distributes the result back to all processes.

count.doc: Number of elements (of type `datatype`) to be reduced.

datatype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be reduced.

op.doc: Type of the reduction operation to be performed, see [`cudssOpType_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssoptype-t "cudssOpType_t") for supported values.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssScattervDevice.signature: int cudssScattervDevice(const void * sendbuf, const int * sendcounts, const int * displs, cudssDataType_t sendtype, void * recvbuf, int recvcount, cudssDataType_t recvtype, int root, void * comm, cudaStream_t stream)
cudssScattervDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which scatters a buffer in parts to all processes in a communicator.

sendcounts.doc: Non-negative integer array (of length communicator size) specifying the number of elements to send to each rank.

displs.doc: An array of integers of length communicator size. Entry i specifies the displacement (relative to `sendbuf`) from which to take the outgoing data to process i.

sendtype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be sent.

recvcount.doc: Number of elements in receive buffer (non-negative integer).

recvtype.doc: cuDSS datatype of elements to be received.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssCommSplitDevice.signature: int cudssCommSplitDevice(const void * comm, int color, int key, void * newcomm)
cudssCommSplitDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which creates new communicators based on colors and keys.

comm.doc: A pointer to the communicator to be split.

color.doc: Control of the subset assignment. Processes with the same color are grouped together.

key.doc: Control of the rank assignment. Processes in the new communicator are ordered based on the keys.

newcomm.doc: A pointer to the new communicator defined w.r.t to colors.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssCommFreeDevice.doc: Function pointers to a routine which deallocates resources of a communicator.

comm.doc: A pointer to the communicator to be freed.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssDistributedGetProperty.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which returns a versioning property of the communication layer library.

Used by cuDSS to verify compatibility of a loaded communication layer.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssOpType_t.doc:
The enumerator specifies reduction operation to be used when calling

communication layer APIs `cudssReduce()` or `cudssAllreduce()`.

CUDSS_MAX.doc: Maximum element is found among the reduced elements.

CUDSS_MIN.doc: Minimum element is found among the reduced elements.

cudssThreadingInterface_t.doc:
This struct defines all threading primitives which need to be implemented

in (any) implementation of cuDSS threading layer, see for more details

[threading layer](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#threading-layer-library-in-cudss) and [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).

cudssGetMaxThreads.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which returns the maximum number of threads on the CPU
that can be used by cuDSS for parallel execution.

return_value.doc: The maximum number of threads on the CPU that can be used by cuDSS for parallel execution.

cudssParallelFor.signature: void cudssParallelFor(int nthr_requested, int ntasks, void * ctx, cudss_thr_func_t f)
cudssParallelFor.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which opens a `parallel for` section with the requested number of
threads and call cudss_thr_func_t (see `cudss_threading_interface.h` for details) `f` in
the for loop with ntasks number of iterations.

nthr_requested.doc: Requested number of threads for the parallel section.

ntasks.doc: Number of tasks in the parallel for loop.

ctx.doc:
A pointer to the input data for cudss_thr_func_t `f`

```text
which defines parallel units of work, also called tasks:

void cudss_thr_func_t(*int task*, *void \*ctx*):   Parameters:
    :   * **task** – [in] The task number (or iteration count of the parallel loop).
        * **ctx** – [in] A pointer to the input data.
```

cudssThreadingGetProperty.doc:
A function pointer to a routine which returns a versioning property of the threading layer library.
Used by cuDSS to verify compatibility of a loaded threading layer.

return_value.doc: The error status (as `int`) of the invocation. Must return 0 on success and any nonzero integer otherwise.

cudssCreate.doc:
The function initializes the cuDSS library handle (`cudssHandle_t`) which holds the cuDSS library context.
It allocates light hardware resources on the host, and must be called prior to making any other cuDSS library calls.
Calling any cuDSS function which uses `cudssHandle_t` without a previous call of `cudssCreate()` will return an error.
The cuDSS library context is tied to the current CUDA device. To use the library on multiple devices, one cuDSS handle should be created for each device.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssCreateMg.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssCreateMg(cudssHandle_t * handle, int device_count, const int * device_indices)
cudssCreateMg.doc:
The function initializes the cuDSS library handle (`cudssHandle_t`) which holds the cuDSS library context for multiple devices.
Calling any cuDSS function which uses `cudssHandle_t` without a previous call of `cudssCreateMg()` will return an error.
The cuDSS library context is tied to the CUDA devices defined by `device_count` number and `device_indices` array.
If `device_indices` is `NULL`, cuDSS will take devices from `0` to `device_count - 1`.
The calling device index must be equal to the first device number from `device_indices` or `0` (if `device_indices` is `NULL`)

Note: Same `device_count` and `device_indices` must be passed to [`cudssConfig_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfig-t "cudssConfig_t") object
by calling [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet") with [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_COUNT") and [`CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfigparam-t "CUDSS_CONFIG_DEVICE_INDICES").

Limitations: Some of the features are not supported, see [MG mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-mg-mode) for details.

device_indices.doc: [host] Integer array of size `device_count` which stores device indices. If set to `NULL`, device indices from `0` to `device_count - 1` are used.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssDestroy.doc:
The function releases hardware resources used by the cuDSS library.
This function is the last call with a particular handle to the cuDSS library.
Calling any cuDSS function which uses `cudssHandle_t` after `cudssDestroy()` will return an error.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssGetProperty.doc:
The function returns the value of the requested property. Refer to `libraryPropertyType` for supported types.

The enum `libraryPropertyType` is defined in `library_types.h` (standard CUDA header file).
The supported subset of values for cuDSS is.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssSetStream.doc: The function sets the stream to be used by the cuDSS library to execute its routines.

stream.doc: [host] The stream used by the library.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssSetMgStreams.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssSetMgStreams(cudssHandle_t handle, const cudaStream_t * streams, int stream_count)
cudssSetMgStreams.doc:
The function sets per-device streams to be used by the cuDSS library in multi-GPU mode.
This function should be used when the library handle was created with [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg").

Each stream in the array corresponds to a device specified in [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg").
Specifically, `streams[i]` will be used for operations on `device_indices[i]`.

The `stream_count` parameter must match the `device_count` used in [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg").

**Note:** User is responsible for creating and destroying these streams. The streams must remain valid
for the lifetime of the cuDSS handle. cuDSS will not destroy user-provided streams.

**Note:** This function is optional. If not called, cuDSS will create and manage its own internal
per-device streams for multi-GPU operations.

streams.doc: [host] Array of CUDA streams, one per device.

stream_count.doc: [host] Number of streams in the array (must match device_count from [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg")).

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise. Returns an error if `stream_count` does not match the number of devices, if `streams` is NULL, or if the handle was not created with [`cudssCreateMg()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsscreatemg "cudssCreateMg").

cudssSetDeviceMemHandler.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssSetDeviceMemHandler(cudssHandle_t handle, const cudssDeviceMemHandler_t * handler)
cudssSetDeviceMemHandler.doc:
Set the current device memory handler inside the library handle.

If `handler` argument is set to NULL, the library handle will detach its existing memory handler from the library handle.
In case device memory handler needs to be changed after it is set for the first time, previously set device memory handler needs to be detached.

If a cuDSS API which needs to allocate device memory ([`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute")) is called and there is no device memory handler
attached to the library handle at the moment of the call, cuDSS will allocate device memory internally using a default memory handler.

When the device memory handler is set, during calls to the main cuDSS routine [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute")
the library will allocate the necessary device memory using the `device_alloc()` member of the device memory handler struct.
The allocated memory will remain a part of the `cudssData_t` object used in the call until the allocated memory will be deallocated using the `device_free()`
member of the struct when the corresponding [`cudssDataDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdatadestroy "cudssDataDestroy") is called.
As it follows, erroneous behavior is likely to occur if the device memory handler is changed during the lifespan of the `cudssData_t` objects which have
used the library handle.
See [`cudssDeviceMemHandler_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdevicememhandler-t "cudssDeviceMemHandler_t") for further details about `device_alloc()` and `device_free()`.

The internal stream order is established using the user-provided stream set via [`cudssSetStream()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetstream "cudssSetStream").

Note: It is undefined behavior if the library handle is bound to a memory handler and subsequently to another handler (without detaching), or
the library handle outlives the attached memory pool, or the memory pool is not stream-ordered.

handler.doc: [host] The device memory handler that encapsulates the user’s mempool. The struct content is copied internally.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssGetDeviceMemHandler.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssGetDeviceMemHandler(const cudssHandle_t handle, cudssDeviceMemHandler_t * handler)
cudssGetDeviceMemHandler.doc: Get the current device memory handler.

handler.doc: [host] A (deep) copy of the device memory handler that encapsulates the user’s mempool (if it was set) previously via calling [`cudssSetDeviceMemHandler()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudsssetdevicememhandler "cudssSetDeviceMemHandler").

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssSetCommLayer.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssSetCommLayer(cudssHandle_t handle, const char * commLibFileName)
cudssSetCommLayer.doc:
The function sets the communication layer to be used in [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode)

of cuDSS. The set communication layer will be used for all MGMN mode operations where the

modified library handle is involved.

The communication layer must provide communication backends for both device and host memory buffers.

After setting the communication layer, users should set the device communicator via [`cudssDataSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataset "cudssDataSet")

with [`CUDSS_DATA_COMM_DEVICE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_COMM_DEVICE") and the host communicator with [`CUDSS_DATA_COMM_HOST`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdataparam-t "CUDSS_DATA_COMM_HOST").

For more details of when and how this function should be used, see

[MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).

commLibFileName.doc: [host] Library name or path (resolved by the platform dynamic loader, e.g. `dlopen` / `LoadLibrary`). If NULL, the name is read from [CUDSS_COMM_LIB](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode).

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssSetThreadingLayer.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssSetThreadingLayer(cudssHandle_t handle, const char * thrLibFileName)
cudssSetThreadingLayer.doc:
The function sets the threading layer to be used in [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode)
of cuDSS. The set threading layer will be used for all MT mode operations where the
modified library handle is involved.
For more details of when and how this function should be used, see [MT mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).

thrLibFileName.doc: [host] Library name or path (resolved by the platform dynamic loader, e.g. `dlopen` / `LoadLibrary`). If NULL, the name is read from [CUDSS_THREADING_LIB](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-threaded-mt-mode).

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssLoggerSetCallback.doc:
Sets a custom callback function to receive log messages.

The callback is invoked synchronously from the calling thread and must not call any cuDSS API functions (may cause deadlocks).

Note

In [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode), each process has its own independent logger state and callback.
The callback must be set in each process if needed.

callback.doc: [host] Pointer to callback function (see [`cudssLoggerCallback_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssloggercallback-t "cudssLoggerCallback_t")), or NULL to disable.

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success.

cudssLoggerSetFile.doc:
Redirects log output to an already-opened file handle.

Pass `NULL` to disable log output entirely.

Note

The file handle must remain open until another file is set or logging is disabled.
Passing `NULL` disables all log output until a valid file is set.

Note

In [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode), each process must use a different file handle to avoid
corrupted or interleaved output. Multiple processes writing to the same file concurrently is not safe.

file.doc: [host] Pointer to open file with write permission, or `NULL` to disable logging.

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success.

cudssLoggerOpenFile.doc:
Opens a file and redirects log output to it. The file is opened in write mode (“w”), truncating any existing content.

Multiple calls automatically close the previous file. Parent directories must exist beforehand.

Note

In [MGMN mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#multi-gpu-multi-node-mgmn-mode), each process must open a different file to avoid
corrupted or interleaved output. Multiple processes writing to the same file concurrently is not safe.

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success, [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`] if file cannot be opened (permission denied, path not found, etc. are not distinguished).

cudssLoggerSetLevel.doc: Sets the logging level to control which messages are output.

level.doc: [host] Log level. Refer to [cuDSS Logging Features](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/logging.html#cudss-logging-features) for specific logging level values.

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success, [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE`] if level is invalid.

cudssLoggerSetMask.doc: Sets the logging mask for fine-grained control over which log types are output.

mask.doc: [host] Bitwise OR of masks. Refer to [cuDSS Logging Features](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/logging.html#cudss-logging-features) for specific logging mask values.

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success.

cudssLoggerForceDisable.doc:
Permanently and irreversibly disables all logging for the entire process.

Once called, logging cannot be re-enabled for the lifetime of the process.

Note

Once this API is called, disables all existing file sinks and registered callbacks immediately.
This API takes precedence over all logging configurations (environment variables, `cudssLoggerSetLevel()`, `cudssLoggerSetMask()`, etc.).

return_value.doc: [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success.

cudssConfigCreate.doc:
The function initializes the cuDSS config object (`cudssConfig_t`) which holds the settings of the solver related

to solving a specific linear system. It allocates light resources on the host.

To release the allocated memory, [`cudssConfigDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigdestroy "cudssConfigDestroy") must be called.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssConfigDestroy.doc: The function releases the host resources used by the cuDSS config object. Using the config object after this function call can lead to undefined behavior.

config.doc: [host] cuDSS config object to be destroyed.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssConfigSet.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssConfigSet(cudssConfig_t config, cudssConfigParam_t param, const void * value, size_t sizeInBytes)
cudssConfigSet.doc: The function sets a parameter (`cudssConfigParam_t`) to the specified value passed by the pointer.

value.doc: [host] A pointer to the value to be set.

sizeInBytes.doc: [host] Number of bytes to be read from the pointer.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssConfigGet.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssConfigGet(const cudssConfig_t config, cudssConfigParam_t param, void * value, size_t sizeInBytes, size_t * sizeWritten)
cudssConfigGet.doc: The function retrieves value of a parameter (`cudssConfigParam_t`) and saves it to the specified memory location.

param.doc: [host] Parameter to be retrieved from the config.

value.doc: [host] A pointer to the output memory.

sizeInBytes.doc: [host] Number of bytes to be written (for verification).

sizeWritten.doc: [host] Valid only when the return value is [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`]. If `sizeInBytes` is non-zero, then `sizeWritten` is the number of bytes actually written; if `sizeInBytes` is zero: `sizeWritten` is the number of bytes needed to write full contents.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssDataCreate.doc:
The function initializes the cuDSS data object (`cudssData_t`) which holds the internal data (e.g., LU factors arrays)
as well as pointers to user-provided data related to solving a specific linear system.
To release the allocated memory, [`cudssDataDestroy()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdatadestroy "cudssDataDestroy") must be called.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssDataDestroy.doc: The function releases the hardware resources used by the cuDSS data object. Using the data object after this function call can lead to undefined behavior.

data.doc: [host] cuDSS data object to be destroyed.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssDataSet.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssDataSet(const cudssHandle_t handle, cudssData_t data, cudssDataParam_t param, const void * value, size_t sizeInBytes)
cudssDataSet.doc: The function sets a parameter (`cudssDataParam_t`) to the specified value passed by the pointer.

value.doc: [host] A pointer to the value to be set.

sizeInBytes.doc: [host] Number of bytes to be read from the pointer.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssDataGet.doc:
The function retrieves value of a parameter (`cudssDataParam_t`) and saves it to the specified memory location.

The output memory buffer can be either on device or on host, a memory copy will be done if necessary.

param.doc: [host] Parameter to be retrieved from the data object.

value.doc: [host/device] A pointer to the output memory.

sizeInBytes.doc: [host] Number of bytes to be written (for verification).

sizeWritten.doc: [host] Valid only when the return value is [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`]. If `sizeInBytes` is non-zero, then `sizeWritten` is the number of bytes actually written; if `sizeInBytes` is zero: `sizeWritten` is the number of bytes needed to write full contents.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssExecute.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssExecute(cudssHandle_t handle, int phase, const cudssConfig_t config, cudssData_t data, const cudssMatrix_t matrix, cudssMatrix_t solution, const cudssMatrix_t rhs)
cudssExecute.doc:
The function executes a phase of the solution process. Prior to calling `cudssExecute()`,
all objects passed as parameters must already be created and properly initialized.

The simplest possible solution process consists of three main phases,
analysis, factorization, and solve, following one another. During the analysis phase, reordering and symbolic factorization
(preparing the internal data structures) are done.
During the factorization phase, numerical factorization is performed and during the solve phase, the factorization is
used to find the solution to the linear system.

The phases must always happen in the following order:
[`CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING") ->
[`CUDSS_PHASE_SYMBOLIC_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_SYMBOLIC_FACTORIZATION") ->
[`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION") -> (optional)
[`CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_REFACTORIZATION")
-> [`CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE").
The optional refactorization is usually skipped before the first solve.
Re-using the analysis results is supported. Users can change matrix values and only need to run the (re-)factorization and solve phases.

Note: Combining phases is supported as long as the order is followed. As an example, combining
[`CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_REORDERING") | [`CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_SOLVE") will result in an error, while [`CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_ANALYSIS") | [`CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "CUDSS_PHASE_FACTORIZATION") is
allowed. Please review [`cudssPhase_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssphase-t "cudssPhase_t") for the full list of phase parameters.

> During the execution, the solver configuration properties are read from the `config` of type [`cudssConfig_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssconfig-t "cudssConfig_t").
> The internal data structures necessary to keep all data required for solving the system (incl. the factors) are kept as a part of
> `data` object of type [`cudssData_t`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssdata-t "cudssData_t"). Users can change the configuration settings or provide additional data
> parameters (e.g. a user permutation) or query extra information (like memory estimates or number of pivots) before/after the phases of the
> solution process via [`cudssConfigSet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssconfigset "cudssConfigSet"), or
> [`cudssDataGet()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssdataget "cudssDataGet"), respectively.

The data buffers in the matrix objects for the input matrix, solution and right-hand side matrices must hold device-visible data,
unless the [hybrid host/device execution mode](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/advanced_features.html#hybrid-host-device-execute-mode) is enabled.
For the hybrid execute mode, matrix, solution or right-hand side can be passed with host memory pointers.

Note: The function has the following limitations on the `cudssMatrix_t` objects which can be used as call arguments,
in addition to the limitations of the corresponding matrix creation routines (e.g., [`cudssMatrixCreateCsr()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixcreatecsr "cudssMatrixCreateCsr")):

* The system matrix must be sparse (currently, only 3-array CSR format is supported).
* Right-hand side and solution matrices must be dense, with column-major layout.
* The input sparse matrix (in the batch case, each matrix in the batch) must have data consistent with its description
  (incl. offsets and indices, indexing base, matrix type)
* The input sparse matrix (in the batch case, each matrix in the batch) may have unsorted column indices but must not have repeating entries.
* The input sparse matrix in CSR format must have its row offsets array start with the indexing base (0 or 1).
* The input sparse matrix may change for the SOLVE phase (except when hybrid execution mode is used) but for distributed matrices, the range of rows (row distribution)
  must remain the same.
* The input sparse matrix, right hand side and solution must have the same datatypes for values and indices (if applicable).
* For the non-uniform input batches, batches with varying shapes are supported. E.g., `nrows`, `ncols`, `nnz` can be different for each batch instance.
  However, the aggregate number of rows and non-zeroes must not exceed the `INT_MAX` limit.
* In MGMN mode all processes must have valid global `nrows`, `ncols`, `nnz` data for sparse matrices and
  valid global `nrows`, `ncols` and local `ld` for the dense matrices. In the batch case, all processes must additionally have a valid `batchCount`.
* If [`cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetdistributionrow1d "cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d") is not used then in MGMN mode full matrix data
  (for the system’s matrix, solution and right-hand side) must be present on the root process, i.e. process with
  `rank` = 0 in the provided communicator. The other processes may have the data pointers set to `NULL`.

  Otherwise the system’s matrix, solution and right-hand side must be distributed according to the corresponding call to [`cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssmatrixsetdistributionrow1d "cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d").

Note: using the `cudssMatrixViewType_t` parameter when creating the sparse input matrix (or a batch of those), one can pass only a
triangular portion of the matrix without the need to explicitly change the underlying matrix data. E.g., if the `mview` is set to
[`cudssMatrixViewType_t::CUDSS_MVIEW_UPPER`], then during the analysis phase, `cudssExecute()` will ignore all the indices in the lower part of the matrix,
even if the underlying matrix storage represents a full matrix.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixCreateDn.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixCreateDn(cudssMatrix_t * matrix, int64_t nrows, int64_t ncols, int64_t ld, const void * values, cudssDataType_t valueType, cudssLayout_t layout)
cudssMatrixCreateDn.doc:
The function creates a matrix object wrapped around dense matrix data.
The provided data buffer for the matrix values must hold device-visible data.

Note: In MGMN mode all processes must have valid `nrows`, `ncols` and `ld`.

See more limitations for using `cudssMatrix_t` objects in the documentation for the main routine, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn(cudssMatrix_t * matrix, int64_t batchCount, const void * nrows, const void * ncols, const void * ld, const void * const * values, cudssDataType_t integerType, cudssDataType_t valueType, cudssLayout_t layout)
cudssMatrixCreateBatchDn.doc:
The function creates a matrix object wrapped around a batch of dense matrices.
The provided data buffer for the matrix values must contain device-visible pointers to device-visible data.

Note: cuDSS supports non-uniform batches with varying shapes, e.g `nrows`, `ncols`, `ld` can be different for each batch instance.

Note: MGMN mode does not support matrix batches.

See more limitations for using `cudssMatrix_t` objects in the documentation for the main routine, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

nrows.doc: [host] Number of rows for each matrix in the batch.

ncols.doc: [host] Number of columns for each matrix in the batch.

ld.doc: [host] Leading dimension for each matrix in the batch.

values.doc: [device] Pointer to values of each dense matrix in the batch.

integerType.doc: [host] Integer type for scalar arrays (nrows, ncols, ld).

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixCreateCsr.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixCreateCsr(cudssMatrix_t * matrix, int64_t nrows, int64_t ncols, int64_t nnz, const void * rowStart, const void * rowEnd, const void * colIndices, const void * values, cudssDataType_t offsetType, cudssDataType_t indexType, cudssDataType_t valueType, cudssMatrixType_t mtype, cudssMatrixViewType_t mview, cudssIndexBase_t indexBase)
cudssMatrixCreateCsr.doc:
The function creates a matrix object wrapped around sparse matrix data.
The provided data buffers for `rowStart`, `rowEnd`, `colIndices` and `values` can hold either device or host memory pointers.
Passing host memory pointers avoids redundant device-to-host data movements when the data resides on the host.

Note: host memory input for the input matrix is not supported when `batchCount` > 1, when uniform batch options are enabled,
or when [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_BTF_COLAMD") or [`CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/types.html#cudssreorderingalg-t "CUDSS_REORDERING_ALG_COLAMD") is used for reordering.

Note: creating a cudssMatrix_t with CSR format does not perform any data consistency checks and thus currently it is
the caller’s responsibility to have data description parameters matching the data.

Note: In MGMN mode all processes must have valid `nrows`, `ncols`, `nnz` data (in case of distributed matrices,
these should correspond to the global matrix)

See more limitations for using `cudssMatrix_t` objects in the documentation for the main routine, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

offsetType.doc: [host] Offset type (`rowStart` and `rowEnd`) of the matrix.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr(cudssMatrix_t * matrix, int64_t batchCount, const void * nrows, const void * ncols, const void * nnz, const void * const * rowStart, const void * const * rowEnd, const void * const * colIndices, const void * const * values, cudssDataType_t offsetType, cudssDataType_t indexType, cudssDataType_t valueType, cudssMatrixType_t mtype, cudssMatrixViewType_t mview, cudssIndexBase_t indexBase)
cudssMatrixCreateBatchCsr.doc:
The function creates a matrix object wrapped around a batch of sparse matrices (CSR format).
The provided data buffer for `rowStart`, `rowEnd`, `colIndices` and `values` must contain device-visible pointers to device-visible data.

Note: cuDSS supports non-uniform batches with varying shapes, e.g `nrows`, `ncols`, `nnz` can be different for each batch instance.

Note: creating a cudssMatrix_t with a batch of matrices in CSR format does not perform any data consistency checks and thus currently it is
the caller’s responsibility to have data description parameters matching the data.

See more limitations for using `cudssMatrix_t` objects in the documentation for the main routine, [`cudssExecute()`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cudss/functions.html#cudssexecute "cudssExecute").

nrows.doc: [host] Number of rows for each matrix in the batch.

ncols.doc: [host] Number of columns for each matrix in the batch.

nnz.doc: [host] Numbers of non-zeroes for each matrix in the batch.

rowStart.doc: [device] Pointer to row start offsets for each matrix in the batch.

rowEnd.doc: [device] Pointer to row end offsets for each matrix in the batch.

colIndices.doc: [device] Pointer to column indices for each matrix in the batch.

values.doc: [device] Pointer to values of each CSR matrix in the batch.

offsetType.doc: [host] Offset type (`rowStart` and `rowEnd`) of the matrices in the batch.

indexType.doc: [host] Index type of the matrices in the batch.

valueType.doc: [host] Data type of the matrices in the batch.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixDestroy.doc:
The function releases memory associated with the matrix wrapper. As cuDSS matrix objects are only lightweight wrappers around the user data,
the user data remains untouched.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixSetValues.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixSetValues(cudssMatrix_t matrix, const void * values)
cudssMatrixSetValues.doc:
The function resets the pointer to values inside the cuDSS matrix object to the provided buffer.
The provided data buffer must hold device-visible data.

values.doc: [device/host] Buffer with the new matrix values.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixSetBatchValues.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixSetBatchValues(cudssMatrix_t matrix, const void * const * values)
cudssMatrixSetBatchValues.doc:
The function resets the pointer to values inside the cuDSS matrix object to the provided buffer.
The provided data buffer for the matrix values must contain device-visible pointers to device-visible data.

values.doc: [device/host] Pointer to the new values for each dense matrix in the batch.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers(cudssMatrix_t matrix, const void * rowStart, const void * rowEnd, const void * colIndices, const void * values)
cudssMatrixSetCsrPointers.doc:
The function resets the CSR pointers inside the cuDSS matrix object to the provided buffers.
The provided data buffers must hold device-visible data.

rowStart.doc: [device/host] Buffer with the new row start offsets.

rowEnd.doc: [device/host] Buffer with the new row end offsets.

colIndices.doc: [device/host] Buffer with the new column indices.

values.doc: [device/host] Buffer with the new matrix values.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.

cudssMatrixSetBatchCsrPointers.signature: cudssStatus_t cudssMatrixSetBatchCsrPointers(cudssMatrix_t matrix, const void * const * rowStart, const void * const * rowEnd, const void * const * colIndices, const void * const * values)
cudssMatrixSetBatchCsrPointers.doc:

cudssMatrixSetDistributionRow1d.doc:
The function sets the 1D distribution for the matrix (CSR or Dense) for the MGMN mode.
The provided `first_row` and `last_row` must be always 0-based and specify the first and the last (included) row indices of the local matrix on the calling process.
Setting `first_row` > `last_row` means that the local matrix is empty for the calling process.

> Note: input sparse matrix, right-hand-size and solution can have a different (from each other) distribution. For example, only
> the sparse matrix can be distributed, while right-hand-size or solution are not.
>
> Note: if the sparse matrix or right-hand side are distributed with an overlap (between processes) then the overlapped part will be summed up, that is
> the overlapped part will have a contribution from all related processes. if the solution is distributed with overlapping (between processes)
> then the overlapped part will have the same values on corresponding processes.

first_row.doc: [host] first row index of the local matrix on the calling process.

last_row.doc: [host] last row index of the local matrix on the calling process.

return_value.doc: The error status of the invocation. Must return [`cudssStatus_t::CUDSS_STATUS_SUCCESS`] on success and some other status code otherwise.
